headline: CRUDE RUNS TO $93 AS HORMUZ TRAFFIC STAYS THIN
lead: Crude added 2.1% to $93.19 and it isn't demand talking, it's one vessel crossing the Strait of Hormuz Wednesday, stuck below the 10-day average with the Iran-Hormuz cycle still refusing to fully unwind.
teaser: Crude runs to $93.19 on thin Hormuz traffic while diesel sits above $6.50 and grains give back the week's China pop.

one_number.context: That's below the 10-day moving average, the tell that the Iran-Hormuz premium in crude is fresh again, not just carryover from July.

yesterdays_call.note: Corn held $5.29 instead of breaking below $5.27; the summit-fade thesis stalled a penny short of the line.
yesterdays_call.call_line: Called corn down toward $5.27 ($5.29 when the call was made). It closed at $5.2925.

action: Lock diesel needs now; a close above $6.55 on the rack price is the next reason to pre-buy fall fuel, not wait.

sections.title: Crude Runs On Thin Hormuz Traffic
sections.body:
- WTI added 2.1% to **$93.19**, brushing the top half of its 52-week range as Wednesday's Hormuz vessel count stayed stuck below its 10-day average.
- Brent's holding above $102 with Iran talks stalled on conditions, the same on-again standoff that's cycled through crude twice since April.
sections.so_what: Fuel costs are rising into harvest with no clean resolution in sight either way.

sections.title: Grains Give Back More Ground
sections.body:
- Corn held **$5.29**, essentially flat, while beans firmed a nickel to $13.26; neither moved enough to matter after Wednesday's midweek selloff.
- Feedstuffs called traders anxious ahead of the next Trump/Xi meeting, the same summit-fade story that cost corn its China pop Tuesday.
sections.so_what: Grains are stalled waiting on a summit date, not a fundamental.

sections.title: Cattle Grind Higher Again
sections.body:
- Live cattle added 0.9% to **$220.82**, its fourth straight positive session after Monday's placement-driven pop cooled off.
- Feeders slipped 0.3% to $336.40, the divergence that's been the tell all week as the market digests placement numbers.
- No fresh Cattle on Feed data today; this is carryover mechanics, not new news.
sections.so_what: Live cattle strength without feeder confirmation is a fed-cattle story, not a herd-rebuild one.

outside_the_pit.title: White House Denies Diesel Export Ban Amid $6.50 Prices
outside_the_pit.body: The denial came a day after Trump and Bessent left the door open; producers pricing fall diesel should note the policy is still unsettled, not resolved.

watch_list.desc: Weekly Export Sales; beans above 1.5M MT keeps the China-demand leg of the rally credible.
Hormuz vessel count; a rebound above the 10-day average unwinds today's crude premium fast.
Diesel rack price; a close above $6.55 says the export-ban debate is now a cost story, not just talk.

daily_quote.text: Energy and persistence conquer all things.

source_summary: CME/CBOT locked settlement prices; oilprice.com; feedstuffs.com; world-grain.com; thefencepost.com; no-tillfarmer.com
